1	# Review: Supertraining Chapter 1 (41 entries + `_book.md`)
2	
3	Reviewer: Claude Opus (independent falsification pass), 2026-09-26.
4	Brief: `staging/review_book_prompt.md`. Standards: `docs/ATOMIZE_BRIEF.md`.
5	Scope: `staging/library/strength-and-conditioning/supertraining--verkhoshansky/*.md`.
6	Source: `staging/books/supertraining-6th-expanded.pdf`, printed pp. 1-94.
7	
8	## How the source was checked
9	
10	- Every entry was compared with the full Chapter 1 text (extracted `st_full.json`, idx 12-104, read in full) and the tables and figures were checked on the page image: Table 1.1 (viewer p. 23), Table 1.2 (viewer p. 37), Table 1.4 (viewer p. 93), the strength-deficit paragraphs (viewer pp. 21-22), Greene & McMahon and the 15-120 ms passage (viewer p. 59), Figs 1.27-1.29 (viewer pp. 75-76), and the chapter opening (viewer p. 13).
11	- **Locator convention.** The entries' "PDF p. N" is the extractor's 0-based index: printed + 11. A normal 1-based PDF viewer (and the Read tool) shows printed page 1 on page 13, so viewer page = printed + 12. Below, "PDF" means the entries' index (printed + 11), to match the entries. The fix is a single note in `_book.md` (row 1), not 41 separate edits.
12	- Rule 4 (When NOT present and substantive) was checked for all 41 entries. All have one. The one that is not really a when-not is `principle--rate-of-force-development` (a "developed later" cross-reference plus an inference); see its row.
13	- Eric's-baseline claims were checked against `docs/method-baseline.md`. Duplicates were checked by grep against `SecondBrain/Knowledge/library` and the staging library.
14	
15	## Global findings (apply to many rows)
16	
17	1. **Unlabeled "Why it works" mechanisms.** About a dozen entries give a mechanism the book does not state, with no label. ATOMIZE_BRIEF rule: write "The author gives no mechanism. Inference: ...". Each case is listed in its row.
18	2. **Author voice.** Many entries write "Verkhoshansky states/argues" for passages that refer to Verkhoshansky in the third person ("developed ... by Verkhoshansky", printed 34; "Verkhoshansky has shown", printed 10; "(Siff, 1998)", printed 35). These passages are in Siff's voice. Correction: write "the authors" or "Verkhoshansky & Siff" unless the text itself names who is speaking.
19	3. **Harmonized source conflicts.** In five places the book contradicts itself and the entry quietly picks one side: the strength-deficit direction, CAR (superficial vs deep), glycogen-only supercompensation, SEC energy storage by fibre type, and the Table 1.1 "6-80" misprint. ATOMIZE_BRIEF says to record both.
20	
21	## Entry table
22	
23	| File | Verdict | Problem (entry vs source, with page) | Exact correction |
24	|---|---|---|---|
25	| `_book.md` | FIX | (a) Offset convention not stated. "PDF idx" = printed + 11 is 0-based; in a 1-based viewer, printed 1 = viewer p. 13 (checked with the Read tool: viewer p. 12 is TOC page "x"). (b) Addendum row "printed 503-591 / PDF 514-591" cannot both hold: printed 591 would be PDF 602 in a 591-page file. (c) The offset note says "Ch4 start region (printed ~190-191 = PDF 201-202)", which contradicts the table (Ch3 125-200, Ch4 201 = PDF 212). # Review: Supertraining Chapter 1 (41 entries + `_book.md`)

Reviewer: Claude Opus (independent falsification pass), 2026-09-26.
Brief: `staging/review_book_prompt.md`. Standards: `docs/ATOMIZE_BRIEF.md`.
Scope: `staging/library/strength-and-conditioning/supertraining--verkhoshansky/*.md`.
Source: `staging/books/supertraining-6th-expanded.pdf`, printed pp. 1-94.

## How the source was checked

- Every entry was compared with the full Chapter 1 text (extracted `st_full.json`, idx 12-104, read in full) and the tables and figures were checked on the page image: Table 1.1 (viewer p. 23), Table 1.2 (viewer p. 37), Table 1.4 (viewer p. 93), the strength-deficit paragraphs (viewer pp. 21-22), Greene & McMahon and the 15-120 ms passage (viewer p. 59), Figs 1.27-1.29 (viewer pp. 75-76), and the chapter opening (viewer p. 13).
- **Locator convention.** The entries' "PDF p. N" is the extractor's 0-based index: printed + 11. A normal 1-based PDF viewer (and the Read tool) shows printed page 1 on page 13, so viewer page = printed + 12. Below, "PDF" means the entries' index (printed + 11), to match the entries. The fix is a single note in `_book.md` (row 1), not 41 separate edits.
- Rule 4 (When NOT present and substantive) was checked for all 41 entries. All have one. The one that is not really a when-not is `principle--rate-of-force-development` (a "developed later" cross-reference plus an inference); see its row.
- Eric's-baseline claims were checked against `docs/method-baseline.md`. Duplicates were checked by grep against `SecondBrain/Knowledge/library` and the staging library.

## Global findings (apply to many rows)

1. **Unlabeled "Why it works" mechanisms.** About a dozen entries give a mechanism the book does not state, with no label. ATOMIZE_BRIEF rule: write "The author gives no mechanism. Inference: ...". Each case is listed in its row.
2. **Author voice.** Many entries write "Verkhoshansky states/argues" for passages that refer to Verkhoshansky in the third person ("developed ... by Verkhoshansky", printed 34; "Verkhoshansky has shown", printed 10; "(Siff, 1998)", printed 35). These passages are in Siff's voice. Correction: write "the authors" or "Verkhoshansky & Siff" unless the text itself names who is speaking.
3. **Harmonized source conflicts.** In five places the book contradicts itself and the entry quietly picks one side: the strength-deficit direction, CAR (superficial vs deep), glycogen-only supercompensation, SEC energy storage by fibre type, and the Table 1.1 "6-80" misprint. ATOMIZE_BRIEF says to record both.

## Entry table

| File | Verdict | Problem (entry vs source, with page) | Exact correction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_book.md` | FIX | (a) Offset convention not stated. "PDF idx" = printed + 11 is 0-based; in a 1-based viewer, printed 1 = viewer p. 13 (checked with the Read tool: viewer p. 12 is TOC page "x"). (b) Addendum row "printed 503-591 / PDF 514-591" cannot both hold: printed 591 would be PDF 602 in a 591-page file. (c) The offset note says "Ch4 start region (printed ~190-191 = PDF 201-202)", which contradicts the table (Ch3 125-200, Ch4 201 = PDF 212). Chapter 1 map and section counts are correct: 6+6+5+1+3+1+3+4+2+2+1+1+2+4 = 41. Chapter 1 text ends printed 93 (idx 104); idx 105 (printed 94) is blank. | Add under the offset line: "PDF page numbers in this book's entries are 0-based extractor indices (printed + 11). In a 1-based PDF viewer, add 12 to the printed page." Correct the Addendum printed range to "503-579 (verify)"; the extractor's last index is 590. Remove or correct the "Ch4 start region ~190-191" clause. |
| `claim--adaptive-reconstruction-vs-supercompensation` | FIX | (1) CAR: the entry says CAR covers "the readily-available (superficial) and emergency (deep) energy sources". The source conflicts with itself: printed 83 (PDF 94) says "the former [superficial] energy source is referred to as the Current Adaptation Reserves", but the Fig 1.39 caption (printed 84, PDF 95) says "The Deep Adaptation Energy is often referred to as the Current Adaptation Reserves (CAR)". (2) The source also conflicts on supercompensation: printed 85 (PDF 96, Platonov) says "supercompensation of some of the energy sources takes place", while printed 88 (PDF 99) says "No supercompensation has yet been observed to occur among any of the other biochemicals". (3) "other biochemicals deplete under strenuous exercise": printed 87-88 says "ATP levels have never been shown to deplete significantly, even after very strenuous exercise". (4) The glycogen-only argument is at printed 87-88 (PDF 98-99), not the cited 83-85. (5) "two specific reasons stated in the text" overclaims: reason 2 comes from the single-factor-model critique in 1.16.3, not from the "adaptive reconstruction" passage. (6) Why it works is the writer's reasoning, unlabeled. | Record both CAR definitions with their pages. Record both supercompensation statements (printed 85 and printed 88). Replace "deplete ... but do not overshoot" with "ATP is never shown to deplete significantly (printed 87-88); no supercompensation is observed for other biochemicals (printed 88)". Change the locator to "PDF pp. 94-99, printed 83-88". Change "two specific reasons stated in the text" to "one reason stated with the term (printed 84), plus the single-factor-model critique (printed 87-88)". Prefix Why it works with "Inference:". |

(3) Modern concurrent-training evidence shows interference mainly for explosive and power outcomes, less for maximal strength. Add to When NOT: "The authors also state ICT's submaximal nature does not develop strength and power enough for strength and speed sports, except possibly early off-season (PDF 91, printed 80)." |
| `claim--differential-tissue-adaptation-rates` | FIX | Text checks out: "muscle tissue adapts to increased loading within several days ... connective tissues ... after several weeks or months" (McDonagh & Davies 1984), avoid impulsive methods in GPP and for novices, at PDF 46 / printed 35. **`proven` rejected:** the claim rests on one 1984 citation, "several days" is imprecise (the same book says hypertrophy takes weeks, printed 61), and the muscle-tendon imbalance idea is plausible but its modern support is mostly adolescent and short-term data. Delete "well-established ... independent of this text" unless a citation is added. |

The caution about the 1500m and "highly determinate nature" is at printed 81. Problems: (1) `contested` reason is "presented as already-questioned". The brief requires the disagreeing modern source. (2) Why it works (plays, huddles, aerobic recovery between bursts) is entirely the writer's reasoning, unlabeled. The author only says averages disguise instant-to-instant demand (printed 81). (3) "**Inference** do not use" is missing its colon. | Contested reason: "Modern measurement puts the aerobic contribution far higher and earlier than these 1970s tables (e.g. Gastin 2001, Sports Med 31:725-741); the authors themselves call the scheme questionable (printed 81)." ## Missing (important Chapter 1 ideas no entry captures)

1. **Reps vs %1RM polynomial** (4th-order fit, R = 0.9997, Figs 1.13-1.14) and the caveats that it varies by lift and training background (PDF 40-41, printed 29-30).
2. **Fluctuating overload vs monotonic overload** and the Milo critique: progressive overload gives diminishing returns, so loading should wave up and down within a rising trend (PDF 100-102, printed 89-91).
3. **MHC IIX overshoot after detraining** (Andersen & Aagaard 2000: IIX fell with training and rose 17% above baseline 3 months after stopping; the authors link it to tapering and caution that subjects were sedentary) (PDF 69, printed 58).
4. **Blood flow and isometric fatigue:** free capillary flow only below about 15% of maximal tension, occlusion above about 50% MVC, and isometric or quasi-isometric holds over about 6 s cause fast ischaemic fatigue (PDF 26-27, printed 15-16).
5. **The eight Russian principles of sports preparation and the three-part session structure** (awareness through structured training; Fig 1.12 sequence), of which only the age table was atomized (PDF 35-37, printed 24-26).

Also noted, lower priority: the pre-tension and reciprocal-inhibition effect (Caiozzo 1982, printed 28); Hakkinen's weeks 12-20 strength gain without fibre hypertrophy and the claimed "futility" of hypertrophy training for elite athletes (printed 59); the testosterone/cortisol ratio (printed 82); the ~0.4 s limit on conscious correction of movement (printed 71).

1	# Review: Supertraining Chapter 2 and Chapter 3 to 3.4.2 (36 entries)
2	
3	Reviewer: Claude Opus (independent falsification pass), 2026-09-27.
4	Brief: `staging/review_book_prompt.md`. Standards: `docs/ATOMIZE_BRIEF.md` (including the Ch1 lessons).
5	Scope: the 36 files in `staging/_scope_supertraining_ch2-3a.txt` (12 Ch2, 24 Ch3a), folder `staging/library/strength-and-conditioning/supertraining--verkhoshansky/`.
6	Source: `staging/books/supertraining-6th-expanded.pdf`, printed pp. 95-166 (entry "PDF" = 0-based index = printed + 11; viewer page = printed + 12).
7	
8	## How the source was checked
9	
10	- The full text of PDF idx 104-179 (printed 93-168) was extracted with PyMuPDF and read in full. Every entry was compared line by line with that text.
11	- Page images opened with the Read tool (viewer pages): 138 (eccentric data, printed 126), 142 (Table 3.1, printed 130), 153 (Table 3.2, printed 141), 168 (power-law equations, printed 156), 172 (Table 3.6 and eqs 3.8-3.9, printed 160), 173 (Tables 3.7-3.8, printed 161), 174 (Gompertz eq 3.10 and constants, printed 162), 177 (PAP load and timing data, printed 165). Everything else was checked on the extracted text only.
12	- Image findings: Table 3.1, Table 3.7, the power-law and Gompertz constants and the age equations match the entries. Table 3.8 prints "Knee flexors and masticating muscles 0.80" (the entry's image correction is right). Table 3.2 ranks **absolute strength first at all three torques** (the four-component entry is wrong). Table 3.6 shows lifting % **above** lab % for children (age 10: lab 42, lifting 59; the age entry reverses this). On viewer 138 the combined-regime force is cropped at the page edge: "(50? N)"; the entry's "506 N" cannot be confirmed. On viewer 177 the text prints "the largest increase (90%)" beside 6.7% and 5.8%; record as printed and mark it a probable misprint (possibly 9.0%).
13	- Eric's-baseline claims were checked against `docs/method-baseline.md`. Duplicates were checked by grep against `SecondBrain/Knowledge/library` and the staging library. All 36 files have the skill's frontmatter keys, and all `[[links]]` resolve to existing files.
14	- Rule 3: no entry in scope is rated `proven`. Three are `contested` (F-V limitations, three-zone curve, PAP contested); all others `supported`.
15	- Rule 4: every entry has a substantive When NOT section.
16	
17	## Global findings (apply to many rows; rows say "G1" etc. instead of repeating)
18	
19	- **G1. Unlabeled invented examples.** 34 of 36 Example sections are the writer's own football or gym scenarios ("A running back's CMJ...", "A cornerback...", "per this claim") with no "Inference:" label. ATOMIZE_BRIEF: an invented example must be labeled. Fix: prefix every such Example with "Inference:". Several examples also misstate the source; those are listed in the rows.
20	- **G2. Author voice.** Chapter 2 is written about Verkhoshansky in the third person ("This finding by Verkhoshansky (1961, 1963)", printed 99; "A number of Verkhoshansky's studies", printed 102; "Research by Siff and ... students", printed 102; "Verkhoshansky (1996) distinguishes ... this sort of distinction is avoided", printed 133; "Siff and Medvedev have both suggested", printed 162). Entries 1-12 write "Verkhoshansky states/describes/cites his own". Fix: "the authors" (or "Siff" where the passage argues against Verkhoshansky, printed 133-134, 138-139), per the Ch1 lesson.
21	- **G3. "Eric's baseline:" used for uncited inference.** In several entries (posture, pelvic tilt, head position, four-component, warm-up, sex ratio, RC ancestry, scaling) the text after "Eric's baseline:" is the writer's application, not a line of `method-baseline.md`. Fix: cite the baseline bullet (section plus source file) and put the application after "Inference:".
22	- **G4. Em dashes.** The brief bans em dashes. The six section-header dashes are house format (the Moyer style reference uses them), but the Ch3 entries add about 74 inline em dashes (218 total across 24 files vs 144 headers). Replace inline ones with commas, colons or parentheses.
23	- **G5. Source contradiction: what "absolute strength So" means.** Printed 107 confines "absolute strength" to "maximum involuntary strength (see Ch 1)"; Ch1 (`framework--types-of-maximal-strength`) calls it the involuntary ceiling reachable only by electrical stimulation or reflex; printed 147 says isometric "Fo in this context is not the same as the absolute strength So". Yet Table 3.1 sets loads "as % of So", correlates Fmax with So, and printed 114 and 131 treat So as a measured "strength potential". Record this in the strength-deficit, four-component and heterochronicity entries, and do not equate So with 1RM or an IMTP without saying the book is inconsistent.
24	- **G6. Source contradiction: isometric testing.** Printed 110: isometric and isokinetic dynamometers "are unable to measure functional maximal strength, Rate of Force Development or explosive strength, so it is futile to use them" to identify functional deficiencies. Against that: printed 102 computes explosive strength Se from isometric tension (0.5 Fmax over its time); printed 108 defines IES from an explosive-isometric F-t curve; printed 109 says starting strength "is always produced under conditions of isometric muscle action", which "dispels the opinion that ... isometric training should be completely abandoned"; printed 103 says isometric curves give "a fairly accurate picture of slow movement against very large resistance"; printed 110-112 uses dynamometric and functional profiles (built partly from "explosive-isometric muscular tension", printed 111) to find "which muscle groups are underdeveloped". Both the dynamometry heuristic and the profile entry must record this.

# Review: Supertraining Chapter 2 and Chapter 3 to 3.4.2 (36 entries)

Reviewer: Claude Opus (independent falsification pass), 2026-09-27.
Brief: `staging/review_book_prompt.md`. Standards: `docs/ATOMIZE_BRIEF.md` (including the Ch1 lessons).
Scope: the 36 files in `staging/_scope_supertraining_ch2-3a.txt` (12 Ch2, 24 Ch3a), folder `staging/library/strength-and-conditioning/supertraining--verkhoshansky/`.
Source: `staging/books/supertraining-6th-expanded.pdf`, printed pp. 95-166 (entry "PDF" = 0-based index = printed + 11; viewer page = printed + 12).

## How the source was checked

- The full text of PDF idx 104-179 (printed 93-168) was extracted with PyMuPDF and read in full. Every entry was compared line by line with that text.
- Page images opened with the Read tool (viewer pages): 138 (eccentric data, printed 126), 142 (Table 3.1, printed 130), 153 (Table 3.2, printed 141), 168 (power-law equations, printed 156), 172 (Table 3.6 and eqs 3.8-3.9, printed 160), 173 (Tables 3.7-3.8, printed 161), 174 (Gompertz eq 3.10 and constants, printed 162), 177 (PAP load and timing data, printed 165). Everything else was checked on the extracted text only.
- Image findings: Table 3.1, Table 3.7, the power-law and Gompertz constants and the age equations match the entries. Table 3.8 prints "Knee flexors and masticating muscles 0.80" (the entry's image correction is right). Table 3.2 ranks **absolute strength first at all three torques** (the four-component entry is wrong). Table 3.6 shows lifting % **above** lab % for children (age 10: lab 42, lifting 59; the age entry reverses this). On viewer 138 the combined-regime force is cropped at the page edge: "(50? N)"; the entry's "506 N" cannot be confirmed. On viewer 177 the text prints "the largest increase (90%)" beside 6.7% and 5.8%; record as printed and mark it a probable misprint (possibly 9.0%).
- Eric's-baseline claims were checked against `docs/method-baseline.md`. Duplicates were checked by grep against `SecondBrain/Knowledge/library` and the staging library. All 36 files have the skill's frontmatter keys, and all `[[links]]` resolve to existing files.
- Rule 3: no entry in scope is rated `proven`. Three are `contested` (F-V limitations, three-zone curve, PAP contested); all others `supported`.
- Rule 4: every entry has a substantive When NOT section.

## Global findings (apply to many rows; rows say "G1" etc. instead of repeating)

- **G1. Unlabeled invented examples.** 34 of 36 Example sections are the writer's own football or gym scenarios ("A running back's CMJ...", "A cornerback...", "per this claim") with no "Inference:" label. ATOMIZE_BRIEF: an invented example must be labeled. Fix: prefix every such Example with "Inference:". Several examples also misstate the source; those are listed in the rows.
- **G2. Author voice.** Chapter 2 is written about Verkhoshansky in the third person ("This finding by Verkhoshansky (1961, 1963)", printed 99; "A number of Verkhoshansky's studies", printed 102; "Research by Siff and ... students", printed 102; "Verkhoshansky (1996) distinguishes ... this sort of distinction is avoided", printed 133; "Siff and Medvedev have both suggested", printed 162). Entries 1-12 write "Verkhoshansky states/describes/cites his own". Fix: "the authors" (or "Siff" where the passage argues against Verkhoshansky, printed 133-134, 138-139), per the Ch1 lesson.
- **G3. "Eric's baseline:" used for uncited inference.** In several entries (posture, pelvic tilt, head position, four-component, warm-up, sex ratio, RC ancestry, scaling) the text after "Eric's baseline:" is the writer's application, not a line of `method-baseline.md`. Fix: cite the baseline bullet (section plus source file) and put the application after "Inference:".
- **G4. Em dashes.** The brief bans em dashes. The six section-header dashes are house format (the Moyer style reference uses them), but the Ch3 entries add about 74 inline em dashes (218 total across 24 files vs 144 headers). Replace inline ones with commas, colons or parentheses.
- **G5. Source contradiction: what "absolute strength So" means.** Printed 107 confines "absolute strength" to "maximum involuntary strength (see Ch 1)"; Ch1 (`framework--types-of-maximal-strength`) calls it the involuntary ceiling reachable only by electrical stimulation or reflex; printed 147 says isometric "Fo in this context is not the same as the absolute strength So". Yet Table 3.1 sets loads "as % of So", correlates Fmax with So, and printed 114 and 131 treat So as a measured "strength potential". Record this in the strength-deficit, four-component and heterochronicity entries, and do not equate So with 1RM or an IMTP without saying the book is inconsistent.
- **G6. Source contradiction: isometric testing.** Printed 110: isometric and isokinetic dynamometers "are unable to measure functional maximal strength, Rate of Force Development or explosive strength, so it is futile to use them" to identify functional deficiencies. Against that: printed 102 computes explosive strength Se from isometric tension (0.5 Fmax over its time); printed 108 defines IES from an explosive-isometric F-t curve; printed 109 says starting strength "is always produced under conditions of isometric muscle action", which "dispels the opinion that ... isometric training should be completely abandoned"; printed 103 says isometric curves give "a fairly accurate picture of slow movement against very large resistance"; printed 110-112 uses dynamometric and functional profiles (built partly from "explosive-isometric muscular tension", printed 111) to find "which muscle groups are underdeveloped". Both the dynamometry heuristic and the profile entry must record this.
- **G7. `_book.md` not updated.** The Ch2 and Ch3 rows still read "pending | 0". The brief requires the checkpoint after each chapter or unit. Fix: Ch2 "done | 12"; add a "3 (3.1-3.4.2), printed 125-166, PDF 136-177, done, 24" row.
- **G8. Concurrent writer / out-of-scope files.** The folder grew from 78 to 82 files during this review. It contains entries with chapter 3.4.3, 3.4.5 and 3.4.6 (`claim--irradiation-effect-...`, `claim--multijoint-coordination-...`, `claim--exercise-economy-...`, `heuristic--instruction-type-...`). They are outside this scope and were not reviewed; they are not Ch1 files.

| File | Verdict | Problem (entry vs source, with page) | Exact correction |
|---|---|---|---|
| `framework--force-time-curve-adaptation-pattern-by-movement-type` | FIX | Checked: the four F(t) changes (Fig 2.2) at PDF 109 / printed 98; large-resistance, ballistic, SSC and cyclic sub-patterns at PDF 110-111 / printed 99-100. Problems: (1) Source tension not recorded: the printed-100 summary lists "an increase in the working amplitude of the movement" as part of the general pattern, while the SSC case says the transition "causes some decrease in the working amplitude" (printed 100). (2) The printed 99 three-stage sequence (Fig 2.3: uniform force rise, then peak rise plus shorter duration, then early-force rise) is omitted; it is the book's core longitudinal claim. (3) Why it works: "consistent with well-replicated modern findings that RFD and neural drive improve" has no citation (Ch1 lesson). (4) G1, G2 ("Verkhoshansky cites his own longitudinal data"; Fig 2.2 is one individual, captioned Siff & Verkhoshansky 1999). | Add: "The general summary (printed 100) includes an increase in working amplitude; the SSC case (printed 100) reports a decrease. Both as stated." Add the three-stage sequence with "Fig 2.3, printed 98-99". Delete "well-replicated modern findings" or cite a paper (e.g. Aagaard et al. 2002, J Appl Physiol 93:1318, verify). "The authors report data from one individual (Fig 2.2)". Label Example. |
| `claim--joint-angle-specific-strength-training-narrows-transfer` | FIX | Checked: long-length training transfers uniformly, short-length training gains more but transfers less, larger gain at the trained angle, force-angle curve shape unchanged; Zatsiorsky & Raitsin 1974, Raitsin & Sarsania 1975; all at PDF 113 / printed 102 (not 102-103). Problems: (1) "established empirical regularity from isometric training-at-a-single-angle studies" and When NOT "drawn from isometric single-joint training studies": the text never says the training was isometric; it says "the joint angle at which maximum muscular tension is exerted during training". Label Example. |

## G1-G7 status

- **G1 (unlabeled invented examples).** Applied across all 36 files. Every Example not already
  labeled was prefixed "Inference:" with a closing note that it is not in the source (or, where
  the example restates the book's own worked example, labeled as such instead).

  "the authors" throughout; Siff-writing-about-Verkhoshansky passages (speed-barrier entry,

  drawn from, with the entry's own application moved after a separate "Inference:" label.

  separators ("**What it is** —", etc.) were kept exactly as the vault uses them. All identified

  profile's speed index is itself explosive-isometric data).

  write-ownership (another process/coordinator owns it). Not applied: the coordinator should set
  the Ch2 row to "done | 12" and add the "3 (3.1-3.4.2), printed 125-166, PDF 136-177, done, 24"

  and the review itself flagged it as "(50? N)."

  page the review cited was opened directly and the review's readings (Table 3.1, Table 3.2,
  Table 3.6, Table 3.7/3.8, the Gompertz constants, the age-adjustment equations, and every quoted
  passage) checked out against the page images.

## Missing ideas (not added as new entries; for the next atomizer batch)

Per the review's "Missing" section, none of these were added as new library entries in this pass:

1. **3.3.3 The Effect of Strength on Speed of Muscle Action (printed 149-151).** Newton's-law
   argument that only strength can raise speed; Masalgin's 13%/39%-max and 51%/71%-max data;
   Fig 3.19-3.20 strength-speed correlation rising with load; the (a/Fo) ratio as sport-specific;
   "maximum strength is the main factor determining speed of movement" and the stated paradox.
   (Partially recorded as a tension inside `claim--absolute-leg-strength-connects-to-sprint-speed-only-indirectly-via-jump`,
   now `contested`, but the full 3.3.3 content is not its own entry.)
2. **Early stages of strength training (printed 96-97).** Intermuscular coordination (2-3 weeks),
   intramuscular coordination (4-6 weeks), hypertrophy (6-12 weeks), then stagnation; the
   electrical-stimulation studies showing peak-torque gains "in the absence of any changes in
   neural drive" as a cross-chapter tension with Ch1's neuromuscular-stimulation entry.
3. **2.3.3 Structure of motor abilities (printed 120).** Factor analysis showing the number of
   factors rising with proficiency; most structural change happening early in a career.
4. **Optimal stimulus intensity for reactive work (Fig 3.7-3.8, printed 135-136).** The working
   effect rising with drop energy, plateauing, then falling; training raising the curve and
   shifting the plateau right; check against Ch1's shock-method entry before adding.
5. **Quickness vs. speed of movement detail (printed 138-140).** Quickness displayed fully only
   below ~15% of maximal strength (Verkhoshansky 1973); elementary speed not correlating with
   cyclic locomotion speed (Gorozhanin 1976); initial-acceleration/hip-flexor correlation
   specifically, not the rest of the sprint.

apply (direct tension with current Baylor practice)** —", a parenthetical addition to the standard
header, not inline body text).

1	# Review: Supertraining Chapter 3, 3.4.3 to end (36 entries)
2	
3	Reviewer: Claude Opus (independent falsification pass), 2026-09-27.
4	Brief: `staging/review_book_prompt.md`. Standards: `docs/ATOMIZE_BRIEF.md` (including the Ch1 lessons).
5	Scope: the 36 files in `staging/_scope_supertraining_ch3b.txt`, folder `staging/library/strength-and-conditioning/supertraining--verkhoshansky/`, plus the `_book.md` Ch3 rows from 3.4.3 on.
6	Source: `staging/books/supertraining-6th-expanded.pdf`, printed pp. 166-200. Page convention: entry "PDF p. N" is the 0-based index; PDF idx = printed + 11; viewer page = idx + 1. Every page reference below gives both ("PDF 192 / printed 181").
7	
8	## How the source was checked
9	
10	- Full text of PDF idx 174-212 (printed 163-201) was extracted with PyMuPDF and read in full. Every entry was compared line by line with it.
11	- Page images opened with the Read tool (viewer pages): 181 (Tables 3.10-3.12, printed 169), 191 (3.5.3 end, 3.5.4, 3.5.5 start, printed 179), 199 (Fig 3.35, printed 187), 202-203 (Figs 3.37-3.39, printed 190-191), 205 (printed 193), 208-209 (Figs 3.43-3.45, printed 196-197).
12	- What the images settled: Table 3.10 rows are labelled "I-III" and "MS"; at 67.5 kg MS is 13.1 vs I-III 13.0 (MS higher). Table 3.12 caption reads "kcalories"; front squat elite is 12.7. Johns & Wright figures print as 41 / 35 / 11 / 10% (sum 97%). Fig 3.35: relaxation time about 0.40 s at level 1 falling to about 0.22 s at level 5; contraction time about 0.30 s to about 0.22 s. Fig 3.37 (stretch matrix, shoulder): biceps stretched by shoulder **extension + lateral rotation**; triceps by shoulder **flexion + abduction**. Fig 3.38: biceps stretched by elbow extension + pronation. Fig 3.39: iliopsoas stretched by hip extension + medial rotation. Fig 3.44 (movement matrix): triceps acts in shoulder extension + adduction.
13	- External checks (fetched, not from recall): Herbert, de Noronha & Kamper, Cochrane 2011 (CD004577.pub3; PMID 21735398, dated July 2011; cochrane.org displays the same pub3 as "2022, Issue 4"), results via cochrane.org and the Authors' conclusions via the Europe PMC record; Herzog & Leonard 2000, J Biomech 33:531-542, abstract via full-text PDF. Everything else external below is marked "(verify)".
14	- Vault (`SecondBrain/Knowledge/library`): no Herbert/Cochrane, Valsalva, blindfold, irradiation, stretch-tolerance or Johns & Wright material. Relevant stretching items found: `research-papers/dupuy-2018-...` (stretching did not improve DOMS or fatigue, p. 11), `research-papers/carvalho-2012-...` and `research-papers/chatzopoulos-2014-...` (acute stretching mode effects), Moyer `heuristic--passive-vs-active-rom-decision-rule-sprint` and `heuristic--pails-rails-close-active-passive-gap-sprint` (active-passive gap), `research-papers/collings-2026-...` (non-contact ACL mechanism).
15	- All `[[links]]` in the 36 files resolve. No inline em dashes (headers only). Nobody uses "Eric's baseline:" (no misuse; see G6).
16	- Rule 3: one `proven` (stretch-reflex framework), one `contested` (stretching benefits), four `untested` (no-unsafe-stretch, Olympic lifters, dedicated-stretching, spinal ligaments), the other 30 `supported`.
17	
18	## Global findings (rows cite "G1" etc.)
19	
20	- **G1. Locator errors, 3.5.3-3.5.9.** Several entries are one PDF page off, or cite a page the text is not on. 3.5.4 and 3.5.5 start on PDF 190 / printed 179 (not 189/178); the Magnusson bullet is PDF 192 / printed 181 (not 191); 3.5.9 is PDF 198-199 / printed 187-188 (not 199-201). Rows mark these "locator only" so they can be batched.
21	- **G2. Voice.** "The authors" is used throughout, which the brief allows. But 3.5-3.7 is clearly Siff's text: printed 180 (PDF 191) calls the section "this article", and printed 198 (PDF 209) says "a myotensiometer, which we used ... (Siff, 1986)". Where an entry rests on Siff (1986) or Siff (1987), say it is the author citing his own work. This matters for confidence in the Olympic-lifters, six-parameters and flexibility-definition entries.
22	- **G3. Missing mandatory section.** `claim--irradiation-...` and `claim--hypnosis-...` have no **When to apply** section (the skill schema requires it).
23	- **G4. "The book's own example" used for mixed content.** In several rows the Example adds the writer's material under that label (ligament "acute exposure", spurious tension "same tissue flexibility", movement matrix calf raise and leg curl, no-unsafe-stretch "paired example"). Only the source's words may sit under that label; the rest needs "Inference:".
24	- **G5. Source contradictions not recorded** (each is in its row): Table 3.10 vs printed 168 text; breathing volumes vs the "exhalation always exceeded inhalation" statement (printed 172); Iashvili vs Tumanyan on static stretching and active flexibility (printed 175, 185 vs 186); stretch tolerance with tissue "unaltered" (printed 181) vs elastic/plastic tissue change (printed 176, 179, 180, 181); stretching benefits and warm-up injury claims (printed 163, 176, 185) vs "many athletes dispense entirely with special stretching or even warm-up ... without suffering injury" (printed 192); Fig 3.34 separating ballistic from PNF vs the text making gentle ballistic a PNF subtype (printed 183, 186); triceps stretch text (printed 189) vs its own Figs 3.37 and 3.44; "prior stretching decreases isometric force" (printed 184) vs the force enhancement after stretch in the paper it cites.
25	- **G6. Baseline unused.** No entry cites `docs/method-baseline.md`. Not a defect, and better than misuse. Optional: the baseline line "Injury risk can be reduced, not eliminated ... an explicit refusal to promise injury prevention" (Inferred, class-1 transcript p.4) fits When to apply in the stretching-benefits and dedicated-stretching entries.
26	- **G7. "contested" as a category tag.** `claim--multiarticular-...` (confidence `supported`) and `claim--olympic-lifters-...` (confidence `untested`) carry `contested` in `category`. The brief treats contested as a confidence value that needs a named reason. Either drop the tag or set `confidence: contested` with a reason.
27	- **Improvement over the Ch2-3a batch:** Examples are almost all labelled "Inference:", no inline em dashes, no misused baseline lines. The remaining problems are misreads, locators, unrecorded contradictions and a few unlabeled mechanisms.
28	
29	## The three uncited claims on printed 181 (PDF 192)

32	
33	1. **Steroids disrupt the three-material bone-tendon transition** (`claim--tendon-insertion-...`). No citation in the book. The graded enthesis itself is well described in anatomy (fibrocartilaginous entheses with uncalcified and calcified fibrocartilage zones; e.g. Benjamin et al. 2006, J Anat 208:471, verify). I found no source for the steroid-disrupts-gradient mechanism; the steroid-tendon-rupture association rests mainly on case reports and animal studies (verify). Recommendation: set `confidence: untested` for the steroid clause (or split: `supported` for the graded transition, `untested` for the steroid effect), and keep the "uncited" flag the entry already has.
34	2. **"There is generally no such thing as an unsafe stretch or exercise"** (`heuristic--no-unsafe-stretch-...`). Uncited aphorism. `untested` is right.
35	3. **Russian/Eastern European scientists discourage cycling, push-ups and sit-ups for ROM** (absorbed into `framework--six-parameters-...`). Uncited ("they have discovered"). Treat as `untested` inside that entry. Note the book elsewhere lists cycling as an indirect warm-up that "can often enhance performance" (Franks list, printed 164 / PDF 175).

(4) Omits the amortisation reactive-force figure ("by an average of 25% in the vertical jump", printed 167). (5) G3: no When to apply section. # Review: Supertraining Chapter 3, 3.4.3 to end (36 entries)

Reviewer: Claude Opus (independent falsification pass), 2026-09-27.
Brief: `staging/review_book_prompt.md`. Standards: `docs/ATOMIZE_BRIEF.md` (including the Ch1 lessons).
Scope: the 36 files in `staging/_scope_supertraining_ch3b.txt`, folder `staging/library/strength-and-conditioning/supertraining--verkhoshansky/`, plus the `_book.md` Ch3 rows from 3.4.3 on.
Source: `staging/books/supertraining-6th-expanded.pdf`, printed pp. 166-200. Page convention: entry "PDF p. N" is the 0-based index; PDF idx = printed + 11; viewer page = idx + 1. Every page reference below gives both ("PDF 192 / printed 181").

## How the source was checked

- Full text of PDF idx 174-212 (printed 163-201) was extracted with PyMuPDF and read in full. Every entry was compared line by line with it.
- Page images opened with the Read tool (viewer pages): 181 (Tables 3.10-3.12, printed 169), 191 (3.5.3 end, 3.5.4, 3.5.5 start, printed 179), 199 (Fig 3.35, printed 187), 202-203 (Figs 3.37-3.39, printed 190-191), 205 (printed 193), 208-209 (Figs 3.43-3.45, printed 196-197).
- What the images settled: Table 3.10 rows are labelled "I-III" and "MS"; at 67.5 kg MS is 13.1 vs I-III 13.0 (MS higher). Table 3.12 caption reads "kcalories"; front squat elite is 12.7. Johns & Wright figures print as 41 / 35 / 11 / 10% (sum 97%). Fig 3.35: relaxation time about 0.40 s at level 1 falling to about 0.22 s at level 5; contraction time about 0.30 s to about 0.22 s. Fig 3.37 (stretch matrix, shoulder): biceps stretched by shoulder **extension + lateral rotation**; triceps by shoulder **flexion + abduction**. Fig 3.38: biceps stretched by elbow extension + pronation. Fig 3.39: iliopsoas stretched by hip extension + medial rotation. Fig 3.44 (movement matrix): triceps acts in shoulder extension + adduction.
- External checks (fetched, not from recall): Herbert, de Noronha & Kamper, Cochrane 2011 (CD004577.pub3; PMID 21735398, dated July 2011; cochrane.org displays the same pub3 as "2022, Issue 4"), results via cochrane.org and the Authors' conclusions via the Europe PMC record; Herzog & Leonard 2000, J Biomech 33:531-542, abstract via full-text PDF. Everything else external below is marked "(verify)".
- Vault (`SecondBrain/Knowledge/library`): no Herbert/Cochrane, Valsalva, blindfold, irradiation, stretch-tolerance or Johns & Wright material. Relevant stretching items found: `research-papers/dupuy-2018-...` (stretching did not improve DOMS or fatigue, p. 11), `research-papers/carvalho-2012-...` and `research-papers/chatzopoulos-2014-...` (acute stretching mode effects), Moyer `heuristic--passive-vs-active-rom-decision-rule-sprint` and `heuristic--pails-rails-close-active-passive-gap-sprint` (active-passive gap), `research-papers/collings-2026-...` (non-contact ACL mechanism).
- All `[[links]]` in the 36 files resolve. No inline em dashes (headers only). Nobody uses "Eric's baseline:" (no misuse; see G6).
- Rule 3: one `proven` (stretch-reflex framework), one `contested` (stretching benefits), four `untested` (no-unsafe-stretch, Olympic lifters, dedicated-stretching, spinal ligaments), the other 30 `supported`.

## Global findings (rows cite "G1" etc.)

- **G1. Locator errors, 3.5.3-3.5.9.** Several entries are one PDF page off, or cite a page the text is not on. 3.5.4 and 3.5.5 start on PDF 190 / printed 179 (not 189/178); the Magnusson bullet is PDF 192 / printed 181 (not 191); 3.5.9 is PDF 198-199 / printed 187-188 (not 199-201). Rows mark these "locator only" so they can be batched.
- **G2. Voice.** "The authors" is used throughout, which the brief allows. But 3.5-3.7 is clearly Siff's text: printed 180 (PDF 191) calls the section "this article", and printed 198 (PDF 209) says "a myotensiometer, which we used ... (Siff, 1986)". Where an entry rests on Siff (1986) or Siff (1987), say it is the author citing his own work. This matters for confidence in the Olympic-lifters, six-parameters and flexibility-definition entries.
- **G3. Missing mandatory section.** `claim--irradiation-...` and `claim--hypnosis-...` have no **When to apply** section (the skill schema requires it).
- **G4. "The book's own example" used for mixed content.** In several rows the Example adds the writer's material under that label (ligament "acute exposure", spurious tension "same tissue flexibility", movement matrix calf raise and leg curl, no-unsafe-stretch "paired example"). Only the source's words may sit under that label; the rest needs "Inference:".
- **G5. Source contradictions not recorded** (each is in its row): Table 3.10 vs printed 168 text; breathing volumes vs the "exhalation always exceeded inhalation" statement (printed 172); Iashvili vs Tumanyan on static stretching and active flexibility (printed 175, 185 vs 186); stretch tolerance with tissue "unaltered" (printed 181) vs elastic/plastic tissue change (printed 176, 179, 180, 181); stretching benefits and warm-up injury claims (printed 163, 176, 185) vs "many athletes dispense entirely with special stretching or even warm-up ... without suffering injury" (printed 192); Fig 3.34 separating ballistic from PNF vs the text making gentle ballistic a PNF subtype (printed 183, 186); triceps stretch text (printed 189) vs its own Figs 3.37 and 3.44; "prior stretching decreases isometric force" (printed 184) vs the force enhancement after stretch in the paper it cites.
- **G6. Baseline unused.** No entry cites `docs/method-baseline.md`. Not a defect, and better than misuse. Optional: the baseline line "Injury risk can be reduced, not eliminated ... an explicit refusal to promise injury prevention" (Inferred, class-1 transcript p.4) fits When to apply in the stretching-benefits and dedicated-stretching entries.
- **G7. "contested" as a category tag.** `claim--multiarticular-...` (confidence `supported`) and `claim--olympic-lifters-...` (confidence `untested`) carry `contested` in `category`. The brief treats contested as a confidence value that needs a named reason. Either drop the tag or set `confidence: contested` with a reason.
- **Improvement over the Ch2-3a batch:** Examples are almost all labelled "Inference:", no inline em dashes, no misused baseline lines. The remaining problems are misreads, locators, unrecorded contradictions and a few unlabeled mechanisms.

## The three uncited claims on printed 181 (PDF 192)

The printed-181 bullet list has many uncited lines. Three became entries or parts of entries:

1. **Steroids disrupt the three-material bone-tendon transition** (`claim--tendon-insertion-...`). No citation in the book. The graded enthesis itself is well described in anatomy (fibrocartilaginous entheses with uncalcified and calcified fibrocartilage zones; e.g. Benjamin et al. 2006, J Anat 208:471, verify). I found no source for the steroid-disrupts-gradient mechanism; the steroid-tendon-rupture association rests mainly on case reports and animal studies (verify). Recommendation: set `confidence: untested` for the steroid clause (or split: `supported` for the graded transition, `untested` for the steroid effect), and keep the "uncited" flag the entry already has.
2. **"There is generally no such thing as an unsafe stretch or exercise"** (`heuristic--no-unsafe-stretch-...`). Uncited aphorism. `untested` is right.
3. **Russian/Eastern European scientists discourage cycling, push-ups and sit-ups for ROM** (absorbed into `framework--six-parameters-...`). Uncited ("they have discovered"). Treat as `untested` inside that entry. Note the book elsewhere lists cycling as an indirect warm-up that "can often enhance performance" (Franks list, printed 164 / PDF 175).

(3) Entry says the 8-22% decrease happens "without prior right-arm fatigue"; source gives it "during rhythmic flexing of the right arm", no fatigue condition stated. (4) Omits the amortisation reactive-force figure ("by an average of 25% in the vertical jump", printed 167). (5) G3: no When to apply section. Mukhammedova (1958): left-extensor contraction raised right-flexor strength and speed more than left-flexor contraction; the largest effect came when the additional effort was 25-33% of the right arm's." ## Missing ideas (not added as entries, per instruction)

1. **"Isolation" is load-dependent** (printed 198/PDF 209). "The greater the load, the greater the overflow and the greater the involvement of other muscle groups"; isolation by electrical stimulation, low load, or loadless training develops more hypertrophy than functional strength; palpation vs. EMG/myotensiometer (Siff 1986). Ties the irradiation entry (3.4.3) to exercise selection (3.7).
2. **Overtraining is not an energy sum** (printed 170/PDF 181). Overload vs. overuse types; a few-maximal-attempts workout may cause overload-type overtraining more readily than a longer, moderate-weight workout; overload may come more from stress-raising technique than from load itself; actual work is 5-12 min of a 1.5-2.5 h session. (Partially folded into the exercise-economy entry's When NOT; not made its own entry.)
3. **The other reflexes** (printed 178-179/PDF 189-190). Crossed extensor reflex (0.2-0.5s delay, relevant to unilateral dumbbell work); reciprocal inhibition; rebound (repeated maximal acyclic efforts harder, cyclic easier); local muscle spasm as a "physiological splint."
4. **Multi-directional and rotational stretching** (printed 181, 186/PDF 192, 197). Collagen fibre orientation differs by tissue; "very few rotational stretches about the longitudinal axes of the limbs are ever used"; PNF spiral-diagonal patterns give superior 3D functional ROM. Plus printed 175 (PDF 186): ROM in one direction depends on concurrent movement in another, so single-plane lab ROM measures may be equivocal.
5. **Hormonal state and stretching** (printed 183/PDF 194). Pregnancy, menstruation, exogenous hormones (steroids, cortisone) change collagen mechanics, "so that stretching techniques should be adjusted accordingly" (Viidik, 1973). Partially folded into the steroid entry and the ligament-adaptation entry (both now cite this Viidik line), but not made its own entry.

## Reciprocal-link suggestions (not applied; for whoever owns those files)

- `eccentric-quasi-isometrics-for-active-flexibility-and-starting-strength` (this book, GO, untouched) could add a Related link to Moyer's `heuristic--pails-rails-close-active-passive-gap-sprint` (vault): agreement on end-range isometric loading for active range.
- Moyer's two active-passive entries (vault) could add reciprocal Related links back to this book's `claim--active-flexibility-correlates-more-with-sporting-proficiency-than-passive`.
- Myszka's `framework--newell-interacting-constraints` and `framework--direct-learning-attention-intention-calibration` (vault) could add a reciprocal tension link back to `heuristic--instruction-type-and-verbal-framing-shape-strength-output`.
- Dupuy 2018, Carvalho 2012, Chatzopoulos 2014, Collings 2026 (vault research-papers) could each add a reciprocal link back to the relevant Supertraining entry above.

## Disagreements with the review / judgment calls

- G5 lists eight internal contradictions in the global findings section; the task text asked for "each of the six internal contradictions." All eight were recorded (Table 3.10 vs printed 168 narrative; breathing volumes vs "exhalation always exceeded" statement; Iashvili vs Tumanyan on static/passive stretching and active flexibility; stretch tolerance "unaltered" vs elastic/plastic tissue change (four-page spread); stretching benefits/warm-up-injury claims vs the printed-192 "many athletes dispense entirely... without injury" line; Fig 3.34 separating ballistic from PNF vs the text's PNF-subset claim; triceps text vs its own Figs 3.37 and 3.44; "prior stretching decreases isometric force" vs the force-enhancement finding in the cited paper). Flagging the count discrepancy (six named vs eight recorded) rather than silently dropping two.
- `proven` scope (stretch-reflex entry): kept `confidence: proven` at the frontmatter level with an explicit scope statement in When NOT, per the review's stated option, rather than downgrading the whole entry to `supported`.
- Cold-application slug: not renamed (see Not Applied above); a judgment call to protect write-ownership boundaries over following the review's primary suggestion.
- Six-parameters entry: the cycling/push-up/sit-up clause is marked `untested` inline in its own paragraph, but the entry's overall `confidence: supported` was left unchanged, since only that one clause is uncited; the rest of the six-parameter list rests on named citations (Siff 1986, Beaulieu 1986, Sapega et al. 1981).

## Counts

- 36 scoped files: 5 GO (untouched), 31 FIX (applied). `_book.md`: FIX (applied), 5 locator rows corrected plus the 3.4.4 dedup note.
- Confidence changes: 1 entry moved `supported` -> `untested` (steroid-tendon). 2 entries had a disagreeing `contested` category tag dropped (multiarticular, olympic-lifters); their confidence fields (`supported`, `untested`) were unchanged.
- 2 heavy rewrites (irradiation, history-dependence); 1 `proven`-scoping rewrite (stretch-reflex); 2 missing mandatory sections added (irradiation, hypnosis, both **When to apply**).

- **G1. "Eric's baseline" comparisons are unlabelled prose.** About 25 entries write "Eric's baseline does X ... which maps onto / is consistent with this framework" as plain text. 1	# Review: Old Bull Performance course (Opus, falsification pass)
2	
3	Scope: 37 entries plus `_book.md` in `staging/library/performance-technology-and-leadership/old-bull-performance-course--old-bull/`, and the domain `_domain.md`.
4	Sources opened: all 26 lab PDFs at the Drive root (text extracted with PyMuPDF, page numbers are PDF pages), and the transcripts and summaries for Modules 1 to 4. Module 3 (3A Kaigi, 3B, 3C, 3D, Podcast 3, Webinar 3 Parts I to III) was read in full, transcript and PDF, not only summary.
5	Reviewer: Claude Opus, 2026-09-26. Read-only on entries and sources.
6	
7	## Standards applied
8	
9	- "Page" means PDF page for lab PDFs, and file plus timestamp for transcripts and summaries.
10	- **Quotation rule:** any text in quotation marks must be verbatim (allowing ASR spelling) in a transcript or PDF. Every quoted string in every entry was checked by script against all transcripts, summaries and PDF pages, and every miss was then checked by hand.
11	- **"Per the lesson summary" rule:** a locator that names the summary file ("Lab 3B summary, 01:03 to 02:14") counts as the label. What fails is (a) quoting summary text, and (b) attributing a summary writer's own caveat ("this is an anecdote, not a validated rule") to Weber as if he said it. Case (b) occurs four times and is marked FIX.
12	- **Eric's baseline:** every "Eric's baseline:" line was traced to a line in `docs/method-baseline.md`.
13	- **Style:** the "**What it is** —" heading separator matches the Moyer style reference and is kept. Em dashes in body text are a global fix (see below), not a per-row verdict driver.
14	
15	## Source facts established
16	
17	- **Presenter confirmed: Dr Jason Weber.** Independent of the ASR: `The_Grey_Zone_Workbook.pdf` p.1 ("— Dr Jason Weber"), `Video_Lab_The_Grey_Zone_Summary.pdf` p.1 ("Video Lab Overview | Dr Jason Weber"), `The_False_Promise_of_Technology_without_Discipline_Blog.pdf` p.1 ("Jason Weber argues ... As the creator of SpeedSig"). Podcast 1 transcript 00:00:00 ("I'm Jason Weber") agrees.
18	- **Free Version duplicates confirmed.** SHA-256 of the media: Podcast 1 pair `5cf89df2...`, Lab 1C pair `7d7e636c...`, Lab 2C pair `c935e3c8...`, each identical.
19	- **The PDFs are the only non-ASR source,** and several resolve things the entries left open: the CM² name (Lab_1A blog p.1), the "old Russian" origin of means versus modality (Lab_1A blog p.1), the Beacon category (Grey Zone Workbook p.2), a readiness step-up rule for meeting ownership (Lab_3D_Worksheet p.2). Some PDFs (6A summary, 6B Parts A and B, False Promise blog) are third-person course write-ups ("The speaker reflects...", "Weber argues..."), so quotes from them are course material, not Weber's spoken words. That is acceptable, but it should be noted once in `_book.md`.
20	- **Module 3 verdict:** the Module 3 entries were written from summaries, but they survive a check against the transcripts and PDFs on structure and numbers: the Go/No-Go figures (50 players, under 30 s each, 15 to 17 staff, 20-minute report-back: Kaigi transcript 10:19 to 12:13), the 10-minute decide switch (12:14), the 30-minute diagnose meeting (3B 00:02:19), the 24-hour pre-read and parking lot (Podcast 3 00:07:46, 00:10:50), and the head-physio example (3D 00:02:05). The failures are in attribution: a summary template credited to Weber as "stated directly" (3C), a readiness rule said not to exist when the 3D worksheet gives one, and a practice Weber observed in another coach presented as his own (3D). Durable locators should move to the PDFs: 3a blog (Kaigi prerequisites), 3b cheat sheet (decision-log fields, time boxes), 3c blog and template (amber review "e.g., 48 hours", 2-minute footer), 3D worksheet (progression ladder).

# Review: Old Bull Performance course (Opus, falsification pass)

Scope: 37 entries plus `_book.md` in `staging/library/performance-technology-and-leadership/old-bull-performance-course--old-bull/`, and the domain `_domain.md`.
Sources opened: all 26 lab PDFs at the Drive root (text extracted with PyMuPDF, page numbers are PDF pages), and the transcripts and summaries for Modules 1 to 4. Module 3 (3A Kaigi, 3B, 3C, 3D, Podcast 3, Webinar 3 Parts I to III) was read in full, transcript and PDF, not only summary.
Reviewer: Claude Opus, 2026-09-26. Read-only on entries and sources.

## Standards applied

- "Page" means PDF page for lab PDFs, and file plus timestamp for transcripts and summaries.
- **Quotation rule:** any text in quotation marks must be verbatim (allowing ASR spelling) in a transcript or PDF. Every quoted string in every entry was checked by script against all transcripts, summaries and PDF pages, and every miss was then checked by hand.
- **"Per the lesson summary" rule:** a locator that names the summary file ("Lab 3B summary, 01:03 to 02:14") counts as the label. What fails is (a) quoting summary text, and (b) attributing a summary writer's own caveat ("this is an anecdote, not a validated rule") to Weber as if he said it. Case (b) occurs four times and is marked FIX.
- **Eric's baseline:** every "Eric's baseline:" line was traced to a line in `docs/method-baseline.md`.
- **Style:** the "**What it is** —" heading separator matches the Moyer style reference and is kept. Em dashes in body text are a global fix (see below), not a per-row verdict driver.

## Source facts established

- **Presenter confirmed: Dr Jason Weber.** Independent of the ASR: `The_Grey_Zone_Workbook.pdf` p.1 ("— Dr Jason Weber"), `Video_Lab_The_Grey_Zone_Summary.pdf` p.1 ("Video Lab Overview | Dr Jason Weber"), `The_False_Promise_of_Technology_without_Discipline_Blog.pdf` p.1 ("Jason Weber argues ... As the creator of SpeedSig"). Podcast 1 transcript 00:00:00 ("I'm Jason Weber") agrees.
- **Free Version duplicates confirmed.** SHA-256 of the media: Podcast 1 pair `5cf89df2...`, Lab 1C pair `7d7e636c...`, Lab 2C pair `c935e3c8...`, each identical.
- **The PDFs are the only non-ASR source,** and several resolve things the entries left open: the CM² name (Lab_1A blog p.1), the "old Russian" origin of means versus modality (Lab_1A blog p.1), the Beacon category (Grey Zone Workbook p.2), a readiness step-up rule for meeting ownership (Lab_3D_Worksheet p.2). Some PDFs (6A summary, 6B Parts A and B, False Promise blog) are third-person course write-ups ("The speaker reflects...", "Weber argues..."), so quotes from them are course material, not Weber's spoken words. That is acceptable, but it should be noted once in `_book.md`.

3. **Unused primary PDFs.** No entry cites Lab_1A blog, Lab_1b blog, Lab_2a blog, Lab_3a/3b/3c blogs, the 3c slide template, Lab_3D worksheet, Stacking_Evidence_Blog, Structured_Thinking_Under_Pressure, The_Grey_Zone_Workbook, the Integration workbook, or the Grey Zone summary PDF. The corrections above add the ones that matter.

## Challenge to the atomizer's confidence report (0 contested, 36 of 37 supported)

- **No entry needs `contested`** between library sources. The Menaspa 2017 rolling-averages paper in the vault is about ACWR and injury, a different question, and does not conflict.
- **`supported` holds as the practitioner-course ceiling for the frameworks,** with one change: `heuristic--choose-mentors-with-sport-specific-experience.md` should be `untested` (the entry itself calls it untested opinion, and the rewrite leaves no evidence beyond Weber's view).
- **Embedded anecdotes are mostly flagged, but not all.** Flagged correctly: Kaigi Go/No-Go numbers, calf injuries (review-system, structured-dissent), bone stress (integration), injury-risk case (encoding), pelvis/clam (replace-translation), 40-minute planning meeting (time-box), GPS 1998 (rogers), SpeedSig classification (lead-with). **Not flagged:** the AFL mid-session change (set-communication), the soccer knee and SpeedSig-validated hamstring return (evidence-stacking; the caveat present is the summary writer's, credited to Weber), and the head-physio example (assign-meeting). Corrections above.
- **Commercial interest is under-flagged.** SpeedSig is Weber's product (Podcast 1 00:00:47 to 00:00:53). It supplies the decisive evidence in the evidence-stacking hamstring case, the innovator example in the adoption-curve talk, and the branding of the K–B workbook; the Structured Thinking PDF p.1 describes itself as the basis of a protocol "used in the SpeedSig Primer Course". Only lead-with-the-recipient flags it.
- **Weber's own cited science is unflagged where entries lean on it:** decision fatigue and willpower depletion (Webinar 3 Part I), "research shows that after 15 to 20 minutes, people are off on other tangents" (Podcast 3 00:03:04 to 00:03:11), and neuro-linguistic programming (Webinar 3 Part II 00:05:40). None is sourced; the entries that use them should say so (set-communication, translate-metrics).

## Eric's baseline check

Every "Eric's baseline:" line was traced. All but two are supported by `docs/method-baseline.md`.
- **Not in the baseline (claims about Eric's practice):** (1) capability-audit: "Eric's own gap analysis names the department's reporting model as currently under-specified" (the baseline has this only as Tension #2, the baseline author's observation). (2) meeting-typology: the Inference that the baseline "shows [retrospective review] happening informally". Both are marked FIX above.
- **Inferred course-team positions written as Eric's own:** eras claim ("Eric's own course material states a skepticism"; baseline line 29 is Inferred, speaker unconfirmed), cm2 (Vermeil "compass", line 82, Inferred), monitoring-vs-testing and rolling-baselines (weekly tracking preference, line 47, Inferred), meeting-typology (annual plan, line 149, Inferred). Wording is close to the baseline's own, so these are not verdict-changing, but the promote step should append "(course team, Inferred)" to each.
- **Absence claim stated as baseline fact:** reliability-vs-sensitivity ("no MDC95, SWC, or typical-error figure for mRSI appears anywhere in the reviewed corpus"). Marked FIX.

## Duplicates

Grep of `C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\SecondBrain\Knowledge\library` for kaigi, stoplight, decision gate, decision log, means/modality, evidence stack, measurement vs inference, DIKW, grey zone, rolling average/EWMA, protocol drift, tenth man, adoption curve, knowledge-behaviour, Weber/Old Bull: **no duplicates.** Reciprocal-link suggestions:
- `framework--decision-gate-five-elements` and `framework--stoplight-storytelling-format` ↔ `research-papers/robertson-2017-red-amber-or-green-athlete-monitoring-in-team-sport-the-need-for-decision-support-systems.md`
- `framework--decision-gate-five-elements` ↔ `rehab-and-return-to-play/on-field-rtp--harries/heuristic--75-85-percent-mv-decision-gate.md`
- `heuristic--rolling-baselines-miss-gradual-drift` ↔ `research-papers/menaspa-2017-are-rolling-averages-a-good-way-to-assess-training-load-for-injury-prevention.md` (different question: ACWR)
- `framework--decision-log-owner-action-date-review` ↔ `rehab-and-return-to-play/on-field-rtp--harries/principle--framework-is-a-guide-not-a-protocol.md`

`heuristic--rolling-baselines-miss-gradual-drift` overlaps its parent `framework--monitoring-versus-testing` (same Lab_2c passage). The angle (the mechanism) is distinct once relabeled, so keep it.

## Missing (important ideas no entry captures)

1. **The pre-mortem before a return-to-play sign-off.** "It's four weeks from now. He's reinjured. What happened?" Each person writes independently before discussion; the answers become the contingency plan (Structured_Thinking_Under_Pressure.pdf p.3). The most directly usable RTP tool in the course, and no entry has it.
2. **Stating an out-of-threshold result to the coach as a risk decision.** When a result falls outside the pre-set range, the practitioner tells the coach "this athlete is actually worse than they were last week. Your decision is, do they need to play or not?" (Lab 2E transcript 00:03:00 to 00:03:30). It sets out who owns the risk call when thresholds are breached, which the decision-gate entry does not cover.
3. **Coordination overhead grows with staff size, and nimbleness comes from discipline.** A 10-person team has 45 connection possibilities (Webinar 3 Part I transcript 00:10:08 to 00:10:26); "avoiding structure to stay flexible actually makes you reactive" (00:10:48 to 00:11:04).
4. **Know your people before designing the medical/performance interface.** Complete a K–B "People Profile" for each physio–S&C pair before building any grey-zone model, check high-risk combinations (for example Misaligned × Operator), and revisit after any staff change (The_Grey_Zone_Workbook.pdf pp.1 to 3).
5. **Layered monitoring as a sieve.** In the Go/No-Go meeting, staff observations (warm-up, stretching, speech, behaviour) are layers "like a sieve" so information one layer misses is caught by another (Kaigi transcript 08:36 to 09:12, 11:21 to 12:13). This connects evidence stacking to daily readiness, where Baylor's baseline uses a single mRSI marker.

## Counts

- Entries (37): **GO 10, FIX 27, NO-GO 0.** Of the 27 FIX, 11 are minor (quote wording, a locator, or one mislabeled sentence): decision-gate, decision-pathway, integration, measurement-vs-inference, tech-stack, computer, CPD, review-system, structured-dissent, discipline, protocol-drift. The other 16 change attribution, a claim about the source, or the thesis.
- Index files: `_book.md` FIX, `_domain.md` FIX (minor).

## Overall verdict

**GO AFTER FIXES.** The sources are covered well and the numbers are right: every Go/No-Go, meeting-time and statistics figure checked out, and the Module 3 entries hold up against the transcripts and PDFs. The failures follow the Harries pattern: the entries misdescribe what the author did or did not say. Nine entries claim Weber gave no mechanism, criterion or resolution when the transcript or a PDF shows one (mentors, rogers, strategy, translate-metrics, CPD, review-system, decision-pathway, assign-meeting, knowledge-behaviour's Beacon). Four credit a summary writer's caveat to Weber (evidence-stacking, monitoring-vs-testing, reliability, stoplight). One misstates the source's thesis (mentors). Promote only after the 27 entry fixes, the two index fixes and the three global fixes are applied. The mentors rewrite and the 12% RFD relocation are the two that must not be skipped.

## Important course content missing from the entries (max 5)

1. **HSR delivery-format progression.** HSR moves from structured 100/60 m repeats, to short intervals (10 s/10 s, 15 s/15 s, 20 s/20 s), to small-sided games and skill drills (Part 6 10:17-10:46, 23:14-23:30). This is a reusable progression rule, and it is buried inside the case entries.
2. **Fitting rehab into the team week.** Examples: high/moderate/high weeks, partial training midweek, a heavier modified session at the weekend, a walkthrough before the game (05:04-05:37, 17:40-18:10). Case 4 also cut frequency in week 5 to bridge into a "session comparable to match loads" before RTP week (37:24-38:11). Eric's review needs this for the team-week undulation.
3. **The mid-rehab hamstring checkpoint.** About 85% MV around day 14 is "a sound ceiling until further force production or reactive strength criteria are confirmed, as well as some adequate time for biological healing" (Part 6 20:40-21:02). This time-anchored version of the gate appears only in part, in the Case 2 entry.
4. **Speed prescription in late rehab.** He sets a target time plus a percentage bandwidth, "albeit with a ceiling on what is an acceptable progression for that session", with a walk-back conversation after each rep (Part 3 19:57-20:48). The broken-stride entry misstates the bandwidth as a replacement for the time and omits the ceiling.
5. **The five-element case-review template.** Each case is reviewed on the RTP timeline, loading structure, MV progression, MDSA progression, and sport-skill progression (Part 6 00:39-01:17). It is directly usable as the structure for a Baylor RTP case log.

function resolveOne(slug) {
  const res = [];
  if (stagingMap[slug]) stagingMap[slug].forEach(p => res.push({loc:'staging', rel:p, full: path.join(stagingRoot,p)}));
  if (vaultMap[slug]) vaultMap[slug].forEach(p => res.push({loc:'vault', rel:p, full: path.join(vaultRoot,p)}));
  return res;
}

function checkPair(srcSlug, tgtSlug, tgtAliasSlugs) {
  const srcR = resolveOne(srcSlug);
  const tgtR = resolveOne(tgtSlug);
  if (srcR.length===0) return {status:'SRC_MISSING', srcSlug, tgtSlug};
  if (tgtR.length===0) return {status:'TGT_MISSING', srcSlug, tgtSlug};
  // check each src file for tgt slug mention
  const results = [];
  for (const s of srcR) {
    const content = fs.readFileSync(s.full,'utf8');
    const already = content.includes(tgtSlug) || (tgtAliasSlugs||[]).some(a=>content.includes(a));
    results.push({srcLoc:s.loc, srcRel:s.rel, already});
  }
  return {status:'OK', srcSlug, tgtSlug, tgtLoc: tgtR.map(t=>t.loc+':'+t.rel), results};
}
